info.title: Scraperize API
info.description:
Extract public data from social media platforms as clean JSON. Endpoints are split by platform and by what they return, e.g. `GET /v1/twitter/tweet`.

## Authentication
Send your API key in the `x-api-key` header (or `Authorization: Bearer <key>`). Create keys in your dashboard.

## Credits
Each successful live scrape costs **1 credit**. Credits are prepaid and never expire.

## Caching
Every endpoint accepts an optional `cache_max_age` (`1d`|`3d`|`7d`|`14d`|`30d`). A cache hit within that window is returned for **0 credits**.

## Responses
Success returns `{ "data": …, "meta": { "requestId", … } }`. Errors return `{ "error": { "code", "message", "requestId" } }` with a matching HTTP status. `meta` on a scrape carries `creditsCharged`, `creditsRemaining`, `cached`, and (on a hit) `cachedAt`.

## Rate limits
Requests are limited per team per minute; over the limit returns `429` with a `Retry-After` header.

parameters.name: url
parameters.description: Public tweet permalink, e.g. https://x.com/user/status/1234567890

parameters.description: Return a trimmed-down response: only the focal tweet with essential fields, and no reply thread (`replies`/`replyCount` are omitted).

parameters.name: cache_max_age
parameters.description: Optional. Return a cached result if one this age or newer exists — served for **0 credits** with `meta.cached=true` and `meta.cachedAt`. Otherwise a fresh scrape runs (**1 credit**) and refreshes the cache. Omit to always scrape fresh.

result.title: How to fix your entire life in 1 day

tweets.text: If you get addicted to things easily, good, your problem is aim. Point that same obsession at a skill, your body, or your work for 2 years and people will start calling you "disciplined" instead.

Pick a challenge too big for who you are now. 

That's how people change. A challenge above your level drags the new version of you out.

It will suck. You'll fail constantly. You'll feel like a fraud for months. Your old self will beg you to stay the same.

But if you can pull this off, 10-20 times throughout your life, you will blow past everyone else.

Only public data is returned.

content.title: The preparedness paradox: Wait for “ready,” and it might never come
content.body:
57% of U.S. founders who waited before launching a business wish they’d started sooner.

We surveyed aspiring entrepreneurs and business owners across five countries to find out what holds people back.

The top reasons: not enough money, an idea still taking shape, and not feeling prepared.

They’re the same reasons current founders once gave. But the conditions have changed. 

Most respondents say starting a business is more accessible than ever and requires less formal training or credentials. AI has lowered the cost and complexity. 

Founders aren’t waiting for a plan either. In four of the five countries, around 70% worked through their earliest challenges by trial and error.

Ready isn’t a feeling you arrive at. It’s what happens after you start. 
https://lnkd.in/gMCKE5Yn

comments.text:
The barrier is shifting from capital to conviction.
Execution is becoming the scarcest differentiator.

We couldn’t agree more. Most founders don’t become ready first, they become ready by doing. Every step teaches something you could never learn by waiting. 
And if you’re still hesitating: just keep going. 🙌

Great insights! Many people wait for the perfect time, perfect idea, or perfect preparation before starting. But real growth comes from taking action, learning, and improving along the way.
As a Shopify Developer, I’ve seen many businesses grow by starting small, testing ideas, improving their online store, and focusing on customers. A good store is not built overnight - it’s improved step by step.
The important thing is to start, adapt, and keep moving forward. 🚀

get.description:
Scrapes the videos in a public TikTok collection (`tiktok.com/@user/collection/<name>-<id>`), one page at a time (about 20 per page). Returns the collection (name, total videos, cover, owner) and every video with its description, created date, stats (views, likes, comments, shares, saves, reposts — TikTok rounds large view/like/comment/share counts; saves are exact), author (with stats, also rounded), video details (duration, size, covers, play/download URLs, every rendition, subtitles) or photo-post images, music (with its TikTok sound page and Apple Music / Spotify links), hashtags, mentions, tagged place, effects, stickers, link anchors and flags. Pass the returned `cursor` to get the next page; it is null on the last page.

**Downloading video files:** TikTok only serves `video.playUrl`, `video.downloadUrl` and `video.formats[].url` to requests that send the `Cookie` and `Referer` headers returned in `mediaHeaders` (without them: 403 Access Denied), so these links do not open when pasted into a browser. Send both headers from your code, e.g. `curl -H "Cookie: <mediaHeaders.Cookie>" -H "Referer: <mediaHeaders.Referer>" "<video.playUrl>" -o video.mp4`. Covers, photo-post images, music and subtitles need no headers. Media URLs expire within hours.

**Watermarks:** `playUrl` and every `formats[].url` are watermark-free; `downloadUrl` is TikTok’s download copy with the TikTok logo and @username burned in.

parameters.name: url
parameters.description: The public collection URL, e.g. https://www.tiktok.com/@user/collection/Name-7552294476677466893.

parameters.name: cursor
parameters.description: The `cursor` from the previous response, to get the next page. Omit for the first page.

parameters.name: cache_max_age
parameters.description: Optional. Return a cached result if one this age or newer exists — served for **0 credits** with `meta.cached=true` and `meta.cachedAt`. Otherwise a fresh scrape runs (**1 credit**) and refreshes the cache. Omit to always scrape fresh.

200.description: One page of the collection’s videos.

mediaHeaders.description: Send these headers when downloading video files (playUrl / downloadUrl / formats[].url); TikTok returns 403 without them.

get.description: Scrapes the replies to a comment on a public TikTok video. Pass the video `url` and the comment’s `commentId` (the `id` from `/v1/tiktok/video/comments`). Each reply comes with its id, text, created date, detected language, like count, author (id, secUid, username, nickname, avatar, profile link), who it answers when it’s a reply to another reply (`replyTo`: user id, username, nickname, reply id), whether the creator liked it, TikTok’s labels, photo attachments, sticker (static and animated renditions), emoji tokens, share info (a deep link to the reply) and its parent / reply-to ids — about 20 per page, TikTok’s most-liked replies first, then the newest. Pass the returned `cursor` (with the same url and commentId) to get the next page; it is null on the last page. TikTok can repeat a reply or two at a page boundary, so de-duplicate by `id` when collecting a whole thread. A comment with no replies — or an id TikTok doesn’t know — returns an empty list.

get.description:
Returns the videos TikTok shows for a `hashtag` in a `region` (default NG), up to 30 per page. Includes the hashtag (id, name, description, exact video and view counts, cover and profile images, any pinned announcement) and every video with its description, created date, stats (views, likes, comments, shares, saves, reposts — large view/like/comment/share counts are rounded; saves are exact), author (with stats, also rounded), video details (duration, size, covers, play/download URLs, every rendition, subtitles) or photo-post images, music (with its TikTok sound page and Apple Music / Spotify links), hashtags, mentions, tagged place, effects, stickers, link anchors, AI-generated labels, flags and related searches. `servedRegion` is the region the results are for. Pass the returned `cursor` to get the next page; it is null on the last page.

**About the results:** videos come in TikTok’s ranked order, not a complete or chronological list. A video can occasionally appear on more than one page, and the list ends after a few hundred videos at most, however many use the hashtag. Some hashtags are not available in every region; then the response is a 404 and another `region` may work.

**Downloading video files:** TikTok only serves `video.playUrl`, `video.downloadUrl` and `video.formats[].url` to requests that send the `Cookie` and `Referer` headers returned in `mediaHeaders` (without them: 403 Access Denied). Send both headers from your code, e.g. `curl -H "Cookie: <mediaHeaders.Cookie>" -H "Referer: <mediaHeaders.Referer>" "<video.playUrl>" -o video.mp4`. Covers, photo-post images, music and subtitles need no headers. Media URLs expire within hours.

**Watermarks:** `playUrl` and every `formats[].url` are watermark-free; `downloadUrl` is TikTok’s download copy with the TikTok logo and @username burned in.

Each video comes with its description, created date, language, stats (views, likes, comments, shares, saves, reposts — large view/like/comment/share counts are rounded; saves are exact), author (with stats, also rounded), video details (duration, size, covers, play/download URLs, every rendition, subtitles), music (with its TikTok sound page and Apple Music / Spotify links), hashtags, mentions, tagged place, effects, stickers, link anchors, AI-generated labels, flags and related searches. `servedRegion` is the region the results are for. Pass the returned `cursor` (with the same query and region) to get the next page; it is null on the last page.

**About the results:** TikTok matches loosely, so even an unusual query returns a few close matches. Results can shift slightly between identical searches. Results are videos only; filtering by post date and sorting are not available. Search isn’t available in every region (e.g. the United States); then the response is a 404 and another `region` may work. The first search in a region can take up to about a minute; later ones are much faster.

**Downloading video files:** TikTok only serves `video.playUrl`, `video.downloadUrl` and `video.formats[].url` to requests that send the `Cookie` and `Referer` headers returned in `mediaHeaders` (without them: 403 Access Denied). Send both headers from your code, e.g. `curl -H "Cookie: <mediaHeaders.Cookie>" -H "Referer: <mediaHeaders.Referer>" "<video.playUrl>" -o video.mp4`. Covers, music and subtitles need no headers. Media URLs expire within hours.

**Watermarks:** `playUrl` and every `formats[].url` are watermark-free; `downloadUrl` is TikTok’s download copy with the TikTok logo and @username burned in.

get.description:
Returns the TikToks made with a sound, from the sound's page link (`musicUrl`, e.g. `https://www.tiktok.com/music/That's-Who-I-Praise-7370375686554782506`), about 30 per page in TikTok's order — both videos and photo carousels. Each post has a `type` (`video` or `photo`) and comes with its description, created date, language, stats (views, likes, comments, shares, saves, reposts — large view/like/comment/share counts are rounded; saves are exact), author (with stats, also rounded), video details (duration, size, covers, play/download URLs, every rendition, subtitles) or every carousel image, music (with its TikTok sound page and Apple Music / Spotify links), hashtags, mentions, tagged place, effects, stickers, link anchors, AI-generated labels, flags and related searches. `song` is the sound itself (the same object as `/v1/tiktok/song`). Pass the returned `cursor` (with the same `musicUrl`) to get the next page; it is null on the last page.

TikTok skips a few posts on some pages, so a page can hold fewer than 30. Some sounds aren't available in every country (copyright); then the response is a 404.

**Downloading video files:** TikTok only serves `video.playUrl`, `video.downloadUrl` and `video.formats[].url` to requests that send the `Cookie` and `Referer` headers returned in `mediaHeaders` (without them: 403 Access Denied). Send both headers from your code, e.g. `curl -H "Cookie: <mediaHeaders.Cookie>" -H "Referer: <mediaHeaders.Referer>" "<video.playUrl>" -o video.mp4`. Photo images, covers, music and subtitles need no headers. Media URLs expire within hours.

**Watermarks:** `playUrl` and every `formats[].url` are watermark-free; `downloadUrl` is TikTok's download copy with the TikTok logo and @username burned in.

parameters.description: The sound's TikTok page link: `https://www.tiktok.com/music/<title>-<musicId>` (as in a post's `music.url`).

get.description:
Returns TikTok's trending feed (the Explore page) for a `region`: about 30 posts trending there right now, in TikTok's order. Each post comes with its description, created date, language, content category (`contentCategory`, e.g. Comedy, Food & Drink, Singing & Dancing), stats (views, likes, comments, shares, saves, reposts — large view/like/comment/share counts are rounded; saves are exact), author (with stats, also rounded), video details (duration, size, covers, play/download URLs, every rendition, subtitles), music (with its TikTok sound page and Apple Music / Spotify links), hashtags, mentions, tagged place, effects, stickers, link anchors, AI-generated labels and flags. `servedRegion` is the region the feed is for.

**About the feed:** each call returns a fresh batch of trending posts, so there is no cursor — call again for more. TikTok skips a few posts in some batches, so a batch can hold slightly fewer than 30. The first request for a region can take longer.

**Downloading video files:** TikTok only serves `video.playUrl`, `video.downloadUrl` and `video.formats[].url` to requests that send the `Cookie` and `Referer` headers returned in `mediaHeaders` (without them: 403 Access Denied). Send both headers from your code, e.g. `curl -H "Cookie: <mediaHeaders.Cookie>" -H "Referer: <mediaHeaders.Referer>" "<video.playUrl>" -o video.mp4`. Covers, music and subtitles need no headers. Media URLs expire within hours.

**Watermarks:** `playUrl` and every `formats[].url` are watermark-free; `downloadUrl` is TikTok's download copy with the TikTok logo and @username burned in.

parameters.name: region
parameters.description: The region (country) to get results for, as a two-letter code (ISO 3166-1).

parameters.name: cache_max_age
parameters.description: Optional. Return a cached result if one this age or newer exists — served for **0 credits** with `meta.cached=true` and `meta.cachedAt`. Otherwise a fresh scrape runs (**1 credit**) and refreshes the cache. Omit to always scrape fresh.

mediaHeaders.description: Send these headers when downloading video files (playUrl / downloadUrl / formats[].url); TikTok returns 403 without them.

meta.description: requestId + credit/caching metadata (creditsCharged, creditsRemaining, cached, cachedAt).
